# 般若心經開度

**ID:** X0550
**Volume:** X26
**Category:** 般若部類
**Original Category:** 大小乘釋經部／般若部疏
**Byline:** 明 弘麗著
**Dynasty:** 明
**Date:** 1368–1644
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X0550

## Contributors
- 弘麗 (A000245)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle Cáodòng-school commentary on the *Heart Sūtra* (Xuánzàng's short-recension version, T251 = [KR6c0128](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6c/KR6c0128)) by Luófēng [弘麗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BC%98%E9%BA%97) Hónglì (*floruit* mid-seventeenth century), Cáodòng-school dharma-heir of Xuěguān [雪關智誾](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%9B%AA%E9%97%9C%E6%99%BA%E8%AA%BE) Zhìyín, abbot at Rìqīnshān in Sháozhōu (Guǎngdōng). Preserved in the Wàn xùzàng / *Manji zoku-zō* as X550. One fascicle.

The genre marker — *kāidù* "opening-and-crossing" — adapts the Heart Sūtra's *dù yīqiè kǔè* phrase into a commentary-genre term: the work *opens* the sūtra and *crosses* the reader to the far shore.

**Abstract**

X550 is a primary witness to mid-seventeenth-century Cáodòng-school polemical literature and to the regional Sháozhōu monastic culture of the early-Qīng period. Doctrinally Hónglì's reading is broadly Cáodòng-Chan (the *jiàn xìng chéng fó* frame) but with a strong commitment to integrating *jiào* (doctrinal) study — a position that puts him at odds with the more antinomian Mìyún-[圓悟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%82%9F)-line Línjì revivalists (cf. [通容](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%80%9A%E5%AE%B9) Tōngróng's X548 above) and aligns him with the later early-Qīng *jiàozōng héyī* movement.

The preface's polemic against "novel circumstance-talk" (機語新奇) and "varied tones of writing" (文字別調) is a not-so-veiled critique of the Línjì-revival textual culture of the time, particularly the Mìyún [圓悟](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%9C%93%E6%82%9F) Yuánwù circle's *yǔlù* publishing programme. Hónglì's commitment to substantive *jiào*-grounded Chan reading represents the alternative early-Qīng programme that would eventually dominate the subsequent Chinese Buddhist landscape.

Composition date: no internal dating. The bracket *notBefore* 1640 / *notAfter* 1680 reflects Hónglì's attested mid-seventeenth-century teaching career.
